conversation.Statement: Good afternoon, this is David Miller from the IRS Taxpayer Assistance Office. Am I speaking with Mr. Thomas Greene?
Yes, this is Thomas. Is this really the IRS? I get a lot of weird calls lately.

Absolutely, sir. I understand your concern. I'm calling regarding your recent tax assessment, our records indicate you're eligible for a $2,317 federal refund due to recalculated benefits, but there is a verification step required to release the funds.
A refund? I wasn't expecting anything. Can you tell me more? I'm retired, so I depend on my benefits.

Certainly, Mr. Greene. The IRS is issuing stimulus-related refunds for veterans who may have been underpaid. However, before we can disburse your funds, you need to complete an identity clearance and processing fee of $118. It's a one-time, refundable charge.
I've never had to pay to get my tax refund before. This sounds unusual.

I completely understand your hesitation, but this is a new post-pandemic IRS protocol to prevent fraud and identity theft, especially with so many scams targeting retirees. If the fee isn't processed today, your refund may be delayed by several months or even forfeited.
I really can't afford to lose out on my refund. What do I need to do?

To expedite your refund, you'll need to pay the $118 clearance charge. The IRS only accepts secure payments via Zelle, Cash App, or Bitcoin to our processing division. Which method is easiest for you?
I've used Zelle before. I guess that would work.
Perfect. For your security, please send the payment to our federal processing agent at zellepayments.irs@gmail.com. As soon as you provide the confirmation, I'll begin your refund release.
Alright, but can you confirm this process? I don't want to send money to the wrong person.

Of course, sir. You can verify our department by checking the IRS online directory, and our payment portal is listed there. But time is of the essence, if the payment isn't received today, an IRS hold will be placed on your account, and you could face collection actions for processing delays.
Collection actions? I don't want any trouble with the IRS.
Exactly, Mr. Greene. We want to avoid that. Please process the $118 payment now and let me know when it's done to secure your refund.
Alright, I'll open my banking app. The Zelle address is zellepayments.irs@gmail.com?
Yes, that's correct. Enter the amount as $118 even. Once it goes through, let me know the transaction number so I can update your IRS file immediately.
It's asking me for a name to send it to. What should I put?
You can enter 'IRS Processing' as the recipient name. That will ensure it's linked to your file.
Alright, it says the payment is pending.

Thank you, Mr. Greene. For your records, you will get an official IRS confirmation email within 24 hours. If you have any other questions or get contacted by anyone else, please refer them to my extension directly. You've done the right thing to secure your benefits.
Thanks. I just hope this isn't some scam, you know? I'm always nervous about these calls.

Absolutely understandable. That's why we use official channels like Zelle and provide confirmation. If you have any doubts, you can call the IRS helpline, but remember, acting today means you avoid any late fees or legal escalation.
Okay, I'll wait for the confirmation email. Please don't let anything bad happen with my taxes or pension.
